assumptions: The Oculus Browser and Oculus Desktop are co-deployed on the same host; inference, never a fact.
Any source-side code execution yields an unprivileged local process able to interact with OVRServiceLauncher.exe; inference, never a fact.
The victim opens the attacker-controlled remote page; inference, never a fact.

evidence_quotes.quote: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code.
an attacker could expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process, leading to local privilege escalation.

missing_conditions: Victim interaction with the remote attacker-controlled page in an affected Oculus Browser version
Actual source-side code execution rather than only the described potential
A verified relationship placing the source execution and OVRServiceLauncher.exe on the same host or otherwise establishing target-host reachability
Verification that the source execution context is an unprivileged local process
Affected Oculus Desktop version and required platform and service deployment
Evidence that the browser-originated process can trigger or receive the privileged handle exposed by OVRServiceLauncher.exe
response.reason: CVE-2019-3562 establishes HTML injection in Oculus Browser and only potentially code execution; it does not establish actual execution, a local process context, co-deployment with Oculus Desktop, or access to OVRServiceLauncher.exe. CVE-2021-24038 describes privileged-handle exposure to an unprivileged process and resulting local privilege escalation, but does not state that a browser-originated process can receive or trigger that handle. The edge is therefore a plausible but unverified capability bridge, and cannot enter a strict graph as a supported edge without the missing conditions being confirmed.
